cmc-1962|historian|1962-10-28|how did th.answer: The crisis ended on October 28, 1962, when Khrushchev broadcast a message to Kennedy announcing he had ordered work on the Cuban missile sites stopped and the offensive weapons dismantled, crated, and shipped back to the Soviet Union. Kennedy welcomed the decision as a constructive contribution to peace and treated their exchange of letters as the basis for settling the crisis. However, Soviet documents later revealed that short-range tactical nuclear warheads actually remained in Cuba until December 1, 1962, and U.S. intelligence had never detected them during the crisis.

berlin-1989|historian|1989-11-09|why did.answer: The Wall opened largely by accident, due to a mix-up in communication. The East German regime actually intended to ease pressure with controlled, paperwork-heavy travel starting the next day, but spokesman Günter Schabowski mistakenly announced the new travel rules took effect immediately. That slip, amplified by West German broadcasts, brought crowds to the borders that guards couldn't hold back without bloodshed, and no one gave the order to shoot.
